unreleased: Build script: the scripts package that build.py --target scripts makes for the server now has LF line endings and Unix permissions whatever the Windows checkout stores. Before, install.sh failed on the server with "/bin/bash^M: bad interpreter", and deploy.config.sh and .env would have put a carriage return at the end of every value they hold; the scripts also unpack executable now. .gitattributes keeps shell scripts LF in every checkout

Deployment scripts: install.sh and upgrade.sh no longer download the builds over FTP but unpack the newest backend-*.zip and frontend-*.zip from directories on the same machine (BACKEND_RELEASES_DIR / FRONTEND_RELEASES_DIR in deploy.config.sh, replacing the FTP_* settings), after checking that the archive is a whole zip; upgrade.sh now does that before it stops the service, so a missing or half-uploaded archive no longer leaves the application down

Build script: the zips can be uploaded over SFTP (the OpenSSH sftp command, a key login) by adding an [sftp] section to scripts/build.config.toml, for servers whose firewall blocks the high ports passive FTP needs - the upload then no longer times out after a successful FTP login. FTP stays the default; --no-upload no longer needs the remote paths in the config

Deployment script: nginx now serves /sitemap.xml from the frontend build (sitemap.xml next to index.html, 404 without one) unless the backend has the boards module, which writes its own and keeps being proxied. Before, every application without that module answered the crawlers' sitemap request with a 404 from the backend

The payment gateway can now ask Stripe's checkout for the payer's billing address and keeps the country Stripe reports with the payment (payment.extra["customer_country"], an upper-case ISO code, already visible to the purpose's on_paid hook) - the basis for VAT place of supply, OSS limits and local taxes. It is opt-in per payment (PaymentQuote.require_billing_address); a purpose that does not set it changes nothing.

Add a tickets module (app/modules/tickets), a ticketing system for administrators only (User.is_admin) that stands on its own and extends the contact form and the CRM when they are enabled: a ticket (numbered from 100001, type Issue / Order / General (the default) / Internal, open or closed) has a thread of internal notes, received messages and e-mails sent to the requester, each entry with the time spent on it (summed in the ticket's header), rich-text content with pictures, and private file attachments (pictures inside the text are served from an unguessable public address so the requester's mail client can show them). Tickets come from three sources: typed in by an administrator (optionally linked to a CRM partner), read every TICKETS_POLL_SECONDS from an IMAP mailbox configured in .env (TICKETS_IMAP_*; a new mail opens a ticket and, with the CRM on, is linked to the partner with the sender's address, otherwise to none), and the contact form - with the module enabled, a message also opens a ticket. Every mail about a ticket carries its number in the subject as "[Ticket#100253] - ..." and Reply-To is the mailbox, so an answer that keeps the number is added to that ticket (and reopens it) instead of opening a new one; mail from our own addresses and automatic mail that names no ticket never opens a ticket, and a mail read twice is filed once. The module manifest can now declare hooks (a module takes part in a flow another module owns, called only while it is enabled; the contact form's "contact_form.received" is the first) and background_tasks (started with the application, cancelled on shutdown; the mailbox poller is the first), and send_email takes reply_to, attachments and headers
Add app/services/sql.py with like_pattern(), the escaping of `%`, `_` and the escape character for a "contains" search, shared by modules instead of copied into each (the CRM module uses it now)

Add backend/seed_demo.py, a script that fills the database of the demo pub with made-up data: eight tables, opening hours (Monday to Thursday 11-22, Friday to Sunday 11-23), a standing menu of a Czech inn with eight draught beers, the lunch menus of this week and the next, and the notes under the menus. It leaves tables, hours, notes and a menu the pub has already set up alone (--replace makes the standing menu and notes again), writes the lunch menus afresh and never touches reservations. The reservation e-mails are now signed with the name of the demo pub, Hostinec U Zlatého chmele

Add a pub_menu module (app/modules/pub_menu) for the pub's menus: a standing menu of categories (food or drinks) with items that have a description, EU allergen numbers 1-14, several prices with a portion each (a beer at 0,3 l and 0,5 l) and flags - sold out (shown, marked) and hidden (not shown) - and a lunch menu stored per date (soup, main course, dessert, other; a portion, an allergen list and an optional price per dish) that stays a draft until it is published. Visitors read the standing menu and the lunch menu of a week (Monday to Sunday; how many weeks back and ahead is in backend/modules/pub_menu.json, a week outside is refused) without signing in; drafts, hidden items and hidden categories never reach them. Administrators (this application's own is_admin flag) manage categories and items, put them in order by sending the ids in the new order, store or delete the lunch menu of a date, and set a note shown under each menu. Deleting a category deletes its items and their prices. Prices are two decimals at most, never negative, and go out as plain numbers

Add a table_reservations module (app/modules/table_reservations) for the pub: guests reserve a table for a number of people (the system assigns the smallest free table that seats them; the default stay is 2 hours, the guest may ask for another, and it ends at closing time at the latest) or the whole pub from a chosen time until closing, with no sign-in needed. Between two reservations of one table there must be at least 30 minutes; the whole pub cannot be reserved over any table reservation nor twice in a day, and no table can be reserved while the whole pub is. Opening hours are set per weekday and can be changed once for a single date (closed with a reason visitors see, or other hours); a day with reservations cannot be closed or shortened until the administrator has cancelled each of them one by one, with a message for the guest that goes out in an e-mail (written in the guest's language; a failed e-mail is reported and never undoes the cancellation). Everything that decides on the existing reservations holds one advisory lock, so simultaneous requests cannot slip past each other. Guests get a confirmation with a cancellation link (a button on a page, never a GET) and the pub a notice (BOOKING_NOTIFY_MAIL, else CONTACT_MAIL); a honeypot field and a limit of upcoming reservations per e-mail address slow spam down (there is no rate limiting). Reservations, with the personal data in them, are deleted a configurable number of months after their day (default 12). Texts and limits are in backend/modules/table_reservations.json
